content_voiceover: This slide zeroes in on nodular lymphocyte predominant Hodgkin lymphoma, and the title itself makes the key point: as of the 2022 International Consensus Classification, it's no longer classified as Hodgkin lymphoma at all, it's renamed nodular lymphocyte predominant B-cell lymphoma. The neoplastic cells are lymphocyte predominant cells, nicknamed popcorn cells for their multilobulated nuclei, and they're CD20 positive, CD79a positive, BCL6 positive, but CD15 negative and CD30 negative, a phenotype that looks like a germinal center B-cell rather than a classical Reed-Sternberg cell. Biologically, this entity may sit at one end of a spectrum whose other end is T-cell and histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma, THRLBCL, since both share a B-cell-derived neoplastic clone sitting in a reactive T-cell and histiocyte background, just with different growth patterns. The clinical behavior is generally favorable: an indolent course with good overall prognosis, though patients can have occasional late relapses even a decade out, which the survival curve on this slide illustrates nicely compared to classical Hodgkin lymphoma. About 3 to 5 percent of cases progress to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma over time, which matters for surveillance. And because these are CD20 positive B-cell tumors, not classical Hodgkin, treatment shifts toward rituximab-based systemic regimens: R-AVBD, R-CHOP, or R-CVP, rather than the ABVD-based approach used for classical Hodgkin lymphoma.
keypoints: ICC 2022: NLPHL renamed nodular lymphocyte predominant B-cell lymphoma (NLPBCL)
LP/popcorn cells: CD20+/CD79a+/BCL6+, CD15-/CD30- (B-cell phenotype, not classical HL)
Spectrum with THRLBCL (T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma)
3-5% progress to DLBCL; indolent course but occasional late relapse
Treatment: rituximab-based - R-ABVD, R-CHOP, R-CVP (CD20+ drives anti-CD20 therapy)
keypoint_voiceover: Remember that NLPHL was reclassified by the ICC in 2022 as nodular lymphocyte predominant B-cell lymphoma, dropping the Hodgkin label because the LP or popcorn cells are CD20 positive, CD79a positive, BCL6 positive, and CD15 and CD30 negative, a true B-cell phenotype. It sits on a spectrum with T-cell and histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma, three to five percent progress to DLBCL, and because it's CD20 positive, treatment is rituximab-based: R-ABVD, R-CHOP, or R-CVP.
